title: Batch Generation Pipeline Stepper
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: MicroSims
Batch Generation
AI Skills
Automation
Software Pipelines
description: A p5.js stepper through the eight steps of the microsim-generator batch route. Color and a text tag mark each step as a Python script, the AI agent or the design checkpoint, and a detail panel traces the files each step reads and writes and the step that produced each input.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Dividing batch MicroSim generation between scripts and the AI agent
learningObjectives: The learner will differentiate the steps that a Python utility performs from the step that the AI agent performs, and will trace what each step reads and writes.
prerequisites: The batch pipeline list in Chapter 14

accessibility.notes: Left and right arrow keys change the step; each box carries a text tag (script, agent, checkpoint) so color is not the only cue

controls.label: Show files
controls.purpose: Draw arrows for the files the selected step reads (green) and writes for later steps (purple)

controls.label: Steps 1-8
controls.purpose: Click to select a step; hover for a tooltip with its purpose

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through worked example with concrete file hand-offs
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Process stepper with actor color coding and data-flow tracing
keyQuestions: Which steps have exactly one correct answer, and which need judgment?
Which earlier step produced each file this step reads?
Why does the design checkpoint write no file?
commonMisconceptions: The AI agent writes every file in a MicroSim directory
The status file is typed in by a person
assessmentOpportunities: Label each step with its actor
Trace one file from its writer to every reader
Explain why only step 4 is given to the agent
